steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Film language analysis requires examining how cinematography, mise-en-scene, editing and sound work together to create meaning rather than treating each element in isolation. | Key Fact: A micro-feature is any individual element of film language — a specific shot type, a costume choice, an editing technique or a sound design decision. | Key Fact: Meaning in film is typically created through the interaction of multiple micro-features working in combination within a single sequence. | Key Fact: Denotation refers to the literal content of what is shown and heard; connotation refers to the suggested or associated meanings that arise from those elements.
